title: Get started with rlichess
text: public endpoints can accessed anonymously, configuring Lichess Personal Access Token increases rate limits (30–60 games/second) enables -demand rating history generation. Add token .Renviron file: R code, rlichess automatically picks via lic_token():
code: LICHESS_API_TOKEN="lip_your_personal_access_token_here" lic_token()

code: # Core user profile summary as a 1-row tidy tibble user <- lic_user("h8gi") user %>%   select(username, created_at, play_time_total_hours, count_all)  # Performance ratings across all game types (bullet, blitz, rapid, puzzle, etc.) perfs <- lic_user_perfs("h8gi") perfs  # Daily rating history (dates and rating values) history <- lic_user_rating_history("h8gi", perf_type = "bullet")  # In-depth performance statistics (streaks, best wins, worst losses) stats <- lic_user_perf_stats("h8gi", perf = "bullet")

title: Get started with rlichess
text: Raw API data often contains nested JSON objects unformatted move strings. Layer 2 provides offline transformation functions clean reshape data.

title: Get started with rlichess
text: lic_tidy_games() parses raw game data user-centric perspective: - Converts timestamps standard POSIXct datetime vectors (created_at, last_move_at). - Identifies player’s color (user_color) match result (user_result, win). - Extracts opponent names (opponent_name), opponent ratings (opponent_rating), rating differences (user_rating_diff).
code: games <- lic_tidy_games(raw_games, username = "h8gi")  games %>%   select(id, created_at, user_color, user_result, user_rating, opponent_name, opening.name) %>%   head()

title: Get started with rlichess
text: analyze move--move evaluations, clock times, time management, lic_tidy_moves() unpacks game move strings long-format tibble row corresponds one half-move (ply):
code: moves_df <- lic_tidy_moves(games)  moves_df %>%   filter(game_id == first(game_id)) %>%   select(ply, move_number, color, san, clock, eval) %>%   head(10)

title: Get started with rlichess
text: Summarize performance across different opening variations:
code: opening_stats <- lic_stats_openings(games, min_games = 5) opening_stats

what: R Client and Analysis Tools for Lichess
title: R Client and Analysis Tools for Lichess
text: rlichess modern, tidy R client Lichess API. provides tools fetch, clean, analyze chess games, opening repertoires, user profiles, rating histories, puzzles using standard tidyverse conventions.

title: R Client and Analysis Tools for Lichess
text: rlichess separates data access, cleaning, analytics three distinct layers: Layer 1: API Clients (lic_*): Direct HTTP wrappers corresponding 1--1 official Lichess API endpoints. Layer 2: Tidy Wranglers (lic_tidy_*): Pure offline transformation functions unnest standardize chess data tidy tibbles. Layer 3: Chess Analytics (lic_stats_*): Offline statistics analysis tools (e.g. opening win rates).

title: R Client and Analysis Tools for Lichess
text: Install development version GitHub:
code: # install.packages("pak") pak::pak("h8gi/rlichess")  # or using devtools / remotes devtools::install_github("h8gi/rlichess")

title: R Client and Analysis Tools for Lichess
text: Download recent games, tidy user-centric format, unnest moves long tibble, analyze opening win rates single pipeline:
code: library(rlichess) library(dplyr)  # 1. Fetch recent games from Lichess API raw_games <- lic_games_user("h8gi", perf_type = "bullet", max = 50)  # 2. Tidy into user perspective (dates, win/loss, opponent info) games <- lic_tidy_games(raw_games, username = "h8gi")  # 3. Analyze opening win rates stats <- lic_stats_openings(games, min_games = 3) head(stats)  # 4. Unpack 1-row-per-ply moves for move-by-move analysis moves <- lic_tidy_moves(games) head(moves)
